feedback.problem: A particle moves from the origin with a constant velocity of $(i-2j)\,\text{km/h}.$ Find the distance from the particle to the origin after $5$ hours.
feedback.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant velocity $u,$  the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut,
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=i-2j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=5\,\text{h}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & ={r}_{0}+ut \\  & =(0i+0j)+(i-2j)(5) \\  & =(5i-10j)\,\text{km}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the particle to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|5i-10j| \\  & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(-10)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25+100} \\  & =\sqrt{125} \\  & =5\sqrt{5}\,\text{km}.\end{aligned}
$$
